problem: Rising consumption of sugary drinks and related health effects.
title: Seattle introduces a tax on sweetened beverages
context: Seattle wanted to reduce sugary drink consumption and fund health and education programmes.
action_taken: The city commissioned an evaluation with university and public health partners.
observed_outcome: Prices of taxed drinks rose by almost the full tax, with no effect found on food prices or small business closures. A 2024 study found lower-income households cut purchases by nearly 50 percent versus 18 percent for higher-income ones; self-reported consumption results were less clear.
lessons: Taxes can shift purchases, but effects differ by income and measurement method.
limitations: Consumption findings depend on the data source. Health effects were reported in separate studies and were not verified here.

claims.claim_text: Seattle introduced a tax on sweetened beverages in 2018.
A University of Washington study found lower-income households cut sweetened beverage purchases by nearly 50 percent.
